Dear All!

I would appreciate if someone could help me with the following.

I am currently analyzing data from a primate survey, which was
conducted in western Tanzania. The data analysis itself went all right
however I have two questions:

A) How can I export (and into which program?) the detection function
graph? Is it possible to construct it in Excel or Adobe Illustrator?

B) As I am using Whitesides (1987?) method of establishing the
perpendicular distance to the center of the primate group - by
incorporating average group spread and adding 1/2 of that to the
perpendicular distance measured from line to the first primate - there
is a new source of error which is added(=group spread). (I understand
that the method has some draw backs, however it proved most practical
in dense vegetation.) HOW can I incorporate the variation and its
standard error in DISTANCE. I have been trying to add it as a
multiplier, but I have not managed to keep track of the analysis in
that way and so feel unsure about the results.

Thanking you for any help which might come my way,

Regards
Falk Grossmann
Kigoma
Tanzania

Dear All,

I am analyzing data from a project that examined the differences in avian
densities between native (>2/3 native) and non-native habitat (<1/3
native). We surveyed avian communities over three years with the use of
point transects. I used distance sampling and stratified by habitat to get
a density for each habitat.

I'm trying to determine if I can use distance sampling for another aspect
of the project. There is variation in the percentage of native and
non-native habitat at each point so we also collected vegetation data
corresponding to each point. I would like to examine avian density at
different percentages of native and non-native habitat. The problem is
that I do not have enough data to stratify by points. Can I apply the
detection probability from the habitats (native and non-native) to the
corresponding individual points that fall in those categories to get
densities for individual points? I apologize ahead of time if this is a
ridiculous question, but I'm new to distance sampling and I'm trying to
explore its different applications.

Cheers,
Kristina
